title: Geo-stable traffic slope and tenant cooldown fix
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary:
A gradual cross-region traffic shift (automated slope) exposed a race between the tenant-level KV hot-warm cache reconciliation and the routing layer’s progressive traffic handoff. Several Dedicated customer tenants experienced elevated latencies and intermittent 5xxs during a high-throughput region failover rehearsal. Root cause appears to be a combination of (1) stale prefix state in the KV cache for rehomed tenants, (2) aggressive warmup of batch workers on the target region overwhelming long-tail CPU on older GPU hosts, and (3) routing weight updates that did not pause request draining for tenants with active cache rebuilding.

Immediate impact:
- 12 Dedicated tenants observed 10-60s tail latency spikes and ~0.8% increased error rate for ~45 minutes during the rehearsal.
- One Hosted large-tenant experienced degraded throughput until a manual tenant-level cooldown was applied.

What we did (mitigations applied):
1) Rolled an emergency feature-flag that disables automated warmup burst (flag: warmup.slope_disable) for all Dedicated pools.
2) Ran a targeted KV cache soft-flush for affected tenants (script: gs://redwood-runbooks/kv_soft_flush_v2.sh) to force prefix re-synchronization without full cold rebuild.
3) Applied per-tenant traffic-throttle at the proxy layer (rate-limit 75% of prior steady-state) during the handoff window.
4) Opened priority support comms to impacted customers with interim mitigation notes and ETA for permanent fix.

Root cause analysis (current hypothesis):
- The routing controller’s progressive-slope algorithm updates weights in 100ms steps; it did not coordinate with the KV state machine which expects a tenant to be quiesced for ~30s before a safe prefix swap. This allowed live traffic into a region before the KV cache rebuilt, leading to synchronous blocking on cache misses and CPU pressure.
- Dedicated pool autoscaler allowed worker process spin-up without a staged concurrency cap, producing hot bursts on older hosts.

Proposed permanent fixes (multi-step):
A) Routing-policy change: add a tenant-aware quiesce phase to the slope: when rehoming a tenant, the controller will assign a temporary 0.0 weight and initiate a KV resync callback; only after an explicit KV-ready ack will the slope resume to non-zero weights. (seq: controller change + controller->kv handshake)
B) KV soft-sync improvements: make soft-flush idempotent and add a progress endpoint so the controller can poll readiness rather than relying on timing assumptions.
C) Warmup throttling: implement staged worker ramp with per-host concurrency caps for Dedicated pools older than runtime version X to avoid short-term CPU overcommit.
D) Runbook update: add an explicit checklist for any cross-region handoff that includes KV readiness, worker ramp verification, and customer cooldown commands.

Rollout plan for fixes:
- Phase 1 (Hotfix, today): Controller feature flag to insert KV-readiness pause prior to slope resuming. Canary to 2 small regions (test-bed) then 25% traffic to target region.
- Phase 2 (Next week): Deploy KV soft-sync API and controller polling. Run e2e rehearsal with synthetic tenants.
- Phase 3: Warmup throttling and host-side concurrency guards in runtime-1.21. Target full rollout during low-usage window with staged ramp and two-hour monitoring windows.

Verification & observability changes:
- Add "kv:ready" span to tracing; add tracer-based alerts when kv readiness exceeds 15s during handoff.
- New dashboard tile: tenant handoff health with readiness vs slope progress graph.
- SLO guardrail: block an automated slope if >1% tenants in the region show incomplete KV readiness.

Customer communication and post-ops:
- Sent incident summary + mitigations to affected customers on 2026-03-03 17:30 PT (support thread links embedded below).
- Scheduled customer debrief calls for 2026-03-10 with engineering leads for three largest impacted tenants.

Open tasks / acceptance criteria:
- [ ] Controller feature-flag validated in canary for 48 hours with no regressions.
- [ ] KV soft-sync API merged and load-tested to handle 1k tenant resyncs concurrently.
- [ ] Warmup throttling landed in runtime-1.21 and validated on Dedicated staging hardware.
- [ ] Runbook updated and run two scheduled rehearsals with SRE and Solutions Engineering.
- [ ] Postmortem doc (Confluence) published and linked to ticket.

Long-term follow-ups (future epics):
- Improve model selection for kernel scheduling to reduce CPU tail under short bursts.
- Integrate tenant-priority metadata into routing so critical customers can opt into conservative handoffs.

References and links:
- Runbook (draft): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/geo-handoff-checklist
- KV soft-flush script: gs://redwood-runbooks/kv_soft_flush_v2.sh
- GitHub PR (controller change): https://github.com/redwood-inference/controller/pull/1287
- GitHub PR (kv soft-sync): https://github.com/redwood-inference/kv-service/pull/492
- Incident dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/tenant-handoff-2026-03-03
- Support thread for Tenant ACME Inc: https://support.redwood.ai/t/ACME-12345/hand-off-impact

Notes on risk and rollback:
- Controller handshake introduces a small extra delay at handoff (~5-15s) but prevents heavy synchronous cache rebuilds. Flagged rollout enables immediate rollback by toggling slope-handshake=false.
- KV soft-sync changes are backward compatible; script includes a dry-run mode.

Acceptance criteria for marking Done:
- The controller handshake is enabled by default and has run in at least two canary regions for 72h with no elevated error rates.
- KV soft-sync API is in production and has been exercised by at least three controlled rehomes.
- Runbook updated and ops/reliability teams have run two rehearsal drills.
- Customer feedback indicates the mitigations meet expectation and SLA impacts are closed out.
